LAKE PATITAT
In a number of instances the "possibility" or "fersibility" of a second story trout fishery in Lake Jocassee is discussed in the project documentation. The fantastic success of the SCAR program of trout and baitfish stocking is well documented for the past two years. The fine habitat provide: by Lake Jocassee and its unique cold water has created the most important trout fishery in South Carolina and one of the most productive in the Southeast. With the major cold water habitat reductions caused by the impoundment of Lakes Keowee and Jocassee, this resource has become one of the most valuable in the area. Despite some problems with high mercury levels in certain fishes, the Lake Jocassee fishery has become increasingly popular and is having a significant economic impact on the area. As such, this fishery and the delicate dissolved oxygen budget and summer stratification which support it must be given non-mitigable status for project purposes.
A review has been conducted of the applicant's studies entitled "Potential Impacts of the Bad Creek Project," August 1975. The conclusions drawn is that operation of the project will not effect the lake habitat since Jocassee 1 and 2 are not significantly disturbing lake stratification.
